content.comment_body: I'm having trouble with a [product_name] hardware module, [article_no] version. I can connect and upload the program successfully, but when I attempt an Online Test, I receive a message saying the online and offline programs aren't identical (see attached file). The compare tool doesn't show any difference. I've tried [product_name] software, versions [version_no] 7 and 8, with all available updates, to no avail. The version 6 software doesn't support this hardware. I'm hesitant to re-download the uploaded program as suggested, since I'm not sure it will work without errors, and any failure would be unacceptable.

We aren't able to view the full program. It seems you are also using cursor keys. Are you changing values such as counter contents or timers? I've encountered this error when a parameter value is modified after transferring the program, and then an online test is attempted.
I upload and immediately start the online test without making any further changes. The programs are actually identical. I can attach the program file if required.
Feel free to upload the program; it does no harm to take a look at it.

I only have access to [article_no] and [product_name] software version [version_no]. After changing the hardware to [article_no], transferring the program, and switching the module to RUN, I can perform online tests without any issues. I couldn't find anything unusual in the program.

One more thing I forgot: I tested another [product_name] module ([article_no]). After downloading the previously uploaded program and running the online test, everything worked fine. I also tried both software versions [version_no] 7 and 8 with this other module, and it worked as well. It seems the issue is specific to the module from which I downloaded. The hardware version is [article_no], and it gets detected automatically during upload.
Did you change the hardware type in the program to [article_no] before uploading?

Are you referring to altering the program using pushbuttons on the [product_name]? In any case, I haven't. The module is in RUN mode. I start the upload without creating a new project; after the process, I switch the module back to RUN and start the online test, receiving the warning message. That's all, no further changes.

Hello, If the Online-Test in [product_name] software reports differences between the programs, you may have changed a parameter directly on the hardware. This would explain the discrepancy between what's in the software and what's running on the module. When you upload from the hardware, you get both the program and existing parameters. Here's how to check: 1. Upload the program from the base module, 2. Open both the [product_name] software program and the uploaded one, 3. Use the compare tool in [product_name] software version [version_no] to see differences. This should reveal any changes.
I followed the suggestion and found a difference in text blocks when comparing (see attached file).

Hello, Your screenshot shows that one diagram's message text is empty, while another's contains text. This means the programs differ, and you cannot use online test in this case. If you want to test diagram 3, you need to download it first and then use the online test. Hope this clarifies the issue.
I'm still unsure why this happens. I made two uploads (circuit 1 and 3) just seconds apart, yet they aren't identical.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experiences a problem running the Online Test with a [product_name] hardware module using [product_name] software versions [version_no] 7 and 8. After uploading the program, the software reports differences between the online and offline programs, though the compare tool suggests they're the same. The issue seems related to a specific hardware unit, as other identical modules function correctly. This points to a potential hardware-specific parameter mismatch or a hidden configuration state. The user is hesitant to download back to the module, concerned about possible reliability issues.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] software to accurately show program equivalence after uploading and to allow Online Tests without misleading warnings. They also expect reliable processes for safely downloading and uploading programs between the software and hardware module.
